findings.evidence: In my reading of /tmp/marmorstein-teshuvah_fullend.png and teshuvah_end.png there is a horizontal stroke (patah) under the aleph of the abbreviation, and a mark between bet and aleph. That would make it בָּ״אַ״יְ or similar, not בָּא״יְ. The adjudication explicitly rejected the extra patah, but the low-resolution crops do not settle it.

findings.evidence: In s11, עֲבוֹדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמֶּךָ. ends on a short line, and וְתֶחֱזֶינָה עֵינֵינוּ… starts a new indented paragraph. The XML runs both into a single tei:p.

findings.evidence: In s9, וּמַצְמִיחַ יְשׁוּעָה. ends on a short line and וְנֶאֱמָן אַתָּה starts a new line, so a printed break is likely. The XML has one tei:p.
findings.required_fix: Check the layout and keep the printed break if confirmed.

findings.evidence: The seal ends with U+05C3 SOF PASUQ (׃). Every other seal in the set ends with ASCII ':'. The print shows the same colon mark throughout.

findings.evidence: These match my independent reading of the scans: the heading תְּפִלָּה., the English entry rubric, the large ואני ברב חסדך / בבית אלהים block, Mah Tovu, both verse collections including the repeated Ps 17:6, Ashrei with the marginal קמה, חצי קדיש., the full weekday Amidah (no tal/geshem insertions, matching the print), the inset Kedushah with ח׳/ק׳ in description notes, both Modim columns with the page-6 breaks in both, Elohai Netzor, Yehi Ratzon and the English reader-repeat/Whole Kaddish rubric. I also confirmed these defective forms: וְקֹנֵה, וְלִירוּשָׁלַםִ, וְגֹאֲלִי, דּוֹמֶה.
findings.required_fix: none

findings.rule: Strict canonical URN reuse: a transclusion target must be a URN some project realises
findings.evidence: The index transcludes urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:mah_tovu. The Heidenheim file (entering_synagogue.xml:37) maps only prayer:mah_tovu/mah_tovu and prayer:mah_tovu/varani, never prayer:mah_tovu. Under priority, the target either fails to resolve or pulls in another project's Mah Tovu, which has different verses.
findings.required_fix: Put corresp="urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:mah_tovu" on a prayer-unit milestone or div that covers exactly the Mah Tovu paragraph, with a terminator after it. Alternatively, transclude the two parts as a range.

findings.evidence: The prayer-part is named mah_tovu/varani, but וַאֲנִי transliterates as 'vaani' (aleph is not transliterated, no r). The first part, mah_tovu/mah_tovu, just repeats the parent name.
findings.required_fix: Rename to an incipit such as mah_tovu/vaani (register it; check spellings.yaml). Consider giving the first part an incipit name of its own.

findings.rule: Name by incipit, not by ordinal; one canonical milestone per whole verse
findings.evidence: prayer-part corresp="urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:ashrei/quoted_115_18" uses numbers instead of an incipit. The text is all of Psalms 115:18, yet it carries only seg/@source; no bible verse milestone maps it in this project.
findings.required_fix: Rename to ashrei/vaanachnu. Unless Ps 115:18 is canonically mapped elsewhere in the project, also add chapter 115 / verse 18 milestones with terminators.

findings.rule: A plain numerical citation denotes the Psalm (citation_policy in opening_page_resolutions.json)
findings.evidence: The note for קמה points both @target and tei:ref/@target at bible:psalms/145/1. The marginal label names the chapter, Psalm 145.
findings.required_fix: Set tei:ref/@target to urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:psalms/145. Keep the note anchored at the start of the Psalm.

findings.rule: Explicitly terminate a sequence before a switch of unit type
findings.evidence: The verse-part psalms/55/15/beveit is followed only by bare unit="verse" and unit="chapter" milestones. Under refdb.milestone_terminates, a bare milestone closes only its own unit, so neither closes the verse-part. Its scope ends at mah_tovu/mah_tovu only because of the path-depth fallback (1 '/' ≤ 3). The same applies to psalms/39/13/shimah on line 38, which ends at the next verse milestone.
findings.required_fix: Add <tei:milestone unit="verse-part"/> right after בְּרָגֶשׁ: so the scope does not depend on the fallback.

findings.rule: tei:pb marks a page break where the printed page turns; facs should point at a unique leaf
findings.evidence: Every file opens with a pb for the page it starts on, even when no page turn happens there. Counts: n="3"/n8 seven times; n="4"/n9 eight times; n="5"/n10 seven times (counting the in-text break in tzaddiqim); n="6"/n11 four times plus index line 124. Page 2/n7 appears three times: index lines 95 and 98 and ashrei line 40. The break at index line 98 sits before חצי קדיש., which is still on page 2.
findings.required_fix: Keep one pb per actual page turn: p2 before the heading (index:95), p3 at adonai_sefatai, p4 at selichah, p5 inside tzaddiqim, p6 inside hodaah and inside modim_derabbanan (parallel columns). Remove the rest, or use an @ed second token if the repetition is meant to mark a printing.

findings.rule: A source documentary arrangement should pin to its own realisation (exact file pointer or @project)
findings.evidence: entering_synagogue is transcluded by file pointer (line 93). Ashrei and every Amidah unit are transcluded by bare prayer: URNs with no @project, so the documentary book can resolve to another project's text if priority.transclusion lists one first.
findings.required_fix: Use /prayerbook_for_the_new_year-heidenheim-1965-he/<file> pointers, or add @prayerbook_for_the_new_year-heidenheim-1965-he, for the documentary order.

findings.rule: Every front-matter section and title page is gated on opensiddur:paratext
findings.evidence: Both title pages, the copyright div and the Translator's Preface sit in tei:front without any j:conditional on paratext/title-page or paratext/include.
findings.required_fix: Wrap each titlePage in a title-page gate and each prose div in an include gate. Keep the pb outside the gates.

findings.rule: A titlePage transcribes a printed title leaf and is never invented
findings.evidence: The expanded project writes a tei:titlePage ('Expanded Ashkenazi Mahzor') that no book prints.
findings.required_fix: Replace it with a tei:div/tei:head, or drop it.

findings.rule: Conditions on a running order: when a gate fixes a feature to one value, also j:declare that value inside it
findings.evidence: The weekday-Minchah gate fixes service-time/minha=true, holiday-aggregate/shabbat=false and yom-tov=false, but nothing inside the gate declares them.
findings.required_fix: Add a j:declare of those values directly inside the conditional, with a sibling j:endDeclare before line 239.

findings.rule: Speaker roles use the controlled instruction:role/* vocabulary
findings.evidence: The Reader/Congregation split at Modim uses only tei:head text (חזן/קהל) and free-text descriptions. There is no tei:note type="instruction" with corresp urn:x-opensiddur:instruction:role/reader or role/congregation. The concurrency is stated only in prose.
findings.required_fix: Add role notes carrying those URNs as the first item of each column div, and keep the concurrency description.

findings.evidence: The Hebrew שמונה עשרה sits untagged inside an English instruction (also English index line 95).
findings.required_fix: Wrap it in <tei:foreign xml:lang="he">.

findings.evidence: 'On entering the Synagogue:' says when and what the following passage is, with no computable condition, so it is a description. The source file encodes it as type="instruction"; the expanded index (line 63) encodes the same words as type="description".
findings.required_fix: Use type="description" consistently.

findings.rule: No same-file duplicate canonical identities; repeated text not re-mapped
findings.evidence: Ps 5:8 is mapped once, and its Mah Tovu repeat uses seg/@source. The repeated Ps 17:6 is an inline transclude of psalms/17/6@project. Repeat chapter milestones for 5, 30 and 31 carry no corresp. Both declared verse-parts (55/15/beveit, 39/13/shimah with remainder ki_ger) exist in VERSE_PARTS and follow the incipit rule. BA״Y and ח׳/ק׳ are abbr/expan; כליום is sic/corr.

expanded_recitation_order.status: order correct; one blocking resolution defect and conditional-hygiene gaps

findings.evidence: The order is correct: Ashrei, then Half Kaddish gated on minyan, then the silent Amidah (recitation silent=true, repetition=false) with Kedushat Hashem, Elohai Netzor and Yehi Ratzon. The minyan-gated repetition swaps in Kedushah for Kedushat Hashem, sets Modim and Modim derabbanan side by side, omits the closing personal prayers and ends with Whole Kaddish. Declarations close with sibling j:endDeclare (lines 161, 234). There is no Birkat Kohanim, which is correct for an Ashkenazi weekday Minchah. No English fallback is used for Kaddish.
The prayer:mah_tovu target is not realised by the source project (see guideline finding), so the entering-synagogue sequence is incomplete or resolves to foreign text.
findings.required_fix: Map prayer:mah_tovu in entering_synagogue.xml.

findings.evidence: prayer:kaddish/chatzi and prayer:kaddish/shalem are bare URNs. The Birnbaum dependency is documented only in a sourceDesc note (lines 37-40). I could not check that Birnbaum realises exactly these URNs, or that the settings priority list names hasiddur_hashalem-birnbaum-1949-he with no English project ahead of it.
findings.required_fix: Confirm in refdb and the settings file. Add @hasiddur_hashalem-birnbaum-1949-he if the dependency should be pinned.

findings.evidence: Whole Kaddish sits inside the recitation repetition=true declaration, which scopes Kaddish as part of the Amidah repetition.
findings.required_fix: Move it after j:endDeclare at line 234, still inside the minyan conditional.

findings.evidence: The missing j:declare inside the weekday gate (guideline finding) leaves inner service-time conditions undecided when there is no date.
findings.required_fix: As above.
